papers.title: Oncogenic Role of PLOD3 in Melanoma Progression via Wnt/β-catenin Signaling and Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming.
papers.authors: Xu H, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive malignancy, and treatment strategies remain limited for patients with advanced disease, highlighting the need for a better understanding of the driving mechanisms. This study aimed to identify genes associated with melanoma tumorigenesis, characterize their potential mechanisms, and explore the therapeutic relevance and druggability of selected candidates through experimental and computational approaches. Melanoma-related hub genes were screened by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis. The biological functions of the candidate gene were validated using proliferation and migration assays in melanoma cells. RNA sequencing was applied to investigate the underlying molecular mechanism, whereas CIBERSORT and xCell analyses were used to investigate the relationship between PLOD3 and immune infiltration. Structure-based virtual screening was performed to explore candidate PLOD3-binding compounds. PLOD3, C4orf48, BUB1, and CD300LF were identified as a melanoma-related gene signature, among which PLOD3 exhibited the strongest association with melanoma progression and metastasis. PLOD3 was significantly upregulated in melanoma and positively correlated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signatures across multiple independent cohorts. Loss-of-function experiments revealed reduced proliferation, migration, and invasion of melanoma cells following PLOD3 depletion. PLOD3 expression was also associated with Wnt/β-catenin pathway activity, and treatment with a pharmacological Wnt/β-catenin activator partially restored the cellular phenotypes suppressed by PLOD3 silencing. Furthermore, elevated PLOD3 expression was associated with reduced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Structure-based virtual screening identified four candidate compounds-Rosamultin, Actein, Temsirolimus, and Punicalagin-with strong predicted binding affinity to the catalytic glycosyltransferase (GT) domain of PLOD3, supporting its target potential. PLOD3 functions as a critical driver of melanoma progression by promoting Wnt/β-catenin signaling and shaping an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. These findings identify PLOD3 as a promising therapeutic target and provide candidate compounds for further investigation in melanoma-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets.
papers.authors: Walker SK, van der Veeken J, Rudensky AY, Pritykin Y.
papers.abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

papers.title: Correlative insights into luteolin regulating the macrophage-p53-CCNB1/CDK1 axis associated with cell-cycle control in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu C, Yu C, Gao H, Yang C, Li F, Li W.
papers.abstract: Background The polarization of macrophages and the deactivation of oncogenic pathways within the tumor microenvironment are directly linked to the evolution of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a relatively frequent cancer in the world. Though the exact mechanism is yet unknown, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) may alter p53 activity by secreting cytokines. In contrast, the (tumor protein p53, p53) signaling pathway is frequently functionally compromised in HCC as a result of mutation or epigenetic silencing. It is yet unknown if the natural substance luteolin restores p53 function by controlling macrophage polarization, despite its multi-targeted anti-tumor potential. Objective To clarify the interventional role of luteolin in the evolution of HCC and to uncover the mechanism by which macrophage polarization influences this process via the p53 signaling pathway. Methods The functions of pivotal genes (Cyclin B1,CCNB1), (Cyclin-dependent kinase 1, CDK1), p53 and macrophage polarization-associated factors (Interleukin 6, IL-6), (tumor necrosis factor-α, TNF-α), (Interleukin 10, IL-10), (Transforming growth factor beta 1, TGF-β1) were experimentally verified in conjunction with bioinformatics analysis (screening of luteolin targets for intersection with HCC differential genes and pivotal genes), transcriptome enrichment analysis, immune infiltration assessment, and single-cell sequencing techniques. Results 20 hub genes were screened, 5760 HCC differential genes were found, and 104 luteolin action targets were found. According to enrichment analysis, luteolin inhibited HCC via controlling the metabolism of ROS, extracellular matrix catabolism, and cell cycle pathways (p53, cellular senescence). The presence of M2-type TAMs in the tumor core was confirmed by single-cell sequencing, and their secretion of TGF-β and IL-10 led to aberrant activation of CCNB1/CDK1 and cell cycle dysregulation by promoting the ubiquitylation degradation of p53 and inhibiting its nuclear translocation. Luteolin reversed M2-type macrophage polarization, down-regulated IL-10/TGF-β, and was associated with restoration of p53 function via ATM-dependent p53 phosphorylation. This event may induce G2/M-phase arrest and cellular senescence, as well as suppress the activity of the CCNB1/CDK1 complex. Conclusion Our correlative results suggest that luteolin may reprogram macrophage polarization (inhibiting M2-type and encouraging M1-type), which is associated with relieving IL-10/TGF-β1-mediated suppression of p53 signaling and subsequent inhibition of CCNB1/CDK1-driven cell cycle progression. Nevertheless, the causal direction between macrophage polarization status and p53 function, the primary cellular target of luteolin, protein-level phenotypic validation of macrophage polarization, p53-dependency of CCNB1/CDK1 inhibition, and direct experimental proof for immune escape remain to be fully elucidated. This study highlights the multifaceted impacts of natural medicines in controlling tumor microenvironment and genome stability, and it offers a novel target for combined immune-metabolic therapy of HCC.

papers.title: Thymic single-cell RNA sequencing reveals the immunosuppressive microenvironment in chicken model simulating vertical transmission of recombinant ALV.
papers.authors: Zhang D, Pan Y, Zhong Z, Gu Q, Qiu W, Chen N, Meng K, Gong Z, Zeng Y, Zhao J, Liu P, Wu Y, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Avian leukosis virus (ALV) induces immunosuppression and tumorigenesis. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to analyze the transcriptional dynamics of thymic immune cells in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens, which were intra-embryonic infected with the naturally recombinant ALV-FJ15TH0, at 1-day-old (d), 28d, and 56d post-hatch. Using subgroup-specific marker genes and cell state analysis, we identified six T-cell clusters, two B-cell clusters, and a macrophage cell cluster. Differential gene analysis revealed that ALV infection resulted in a significant enrichment of downregulated genes across all immune cell subsets at 28d. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that ALV infection activated the FoxO immunosuppressive pathway, PI3K pathway, MAPK pathway (CD4 + CD8 + T cells and M2 macrophages at 1d), multicellular synergistic regulation of the cancer pathway (CD4 + CD8 + T cells, M2 macrophages, and Cytotoxic T cells at 28d), and ErbB signaling pathway, Notch signaling pathway (CD4 + CD8 + T cells and M2 macrophages at 56d). Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that ALV infection induced the strongest predicted communication via the PPIA-BSG axis at 28 d. Analysis further inferred that CD147 (BSG) was associated with multiple signaling pathways, including MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT, which may contribute to the immunosuppressive microenvironment. BCL11B, SP3, and EP300 were identified as potential regulatory components with subset-specific associations with JUN, BRAF, and MYB, potentially involving the MAPK, PI3K/AKT, and FoxO signaling pathways. This study reveals the dynamic evolution of the thymic immune microenvironment following ALV-FJ15TH0 infection, providing a resource for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying ALV-induced immunosuppression and offering a foundation for future investigation of its potential relationship with tumorigenesis.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Multi-Omics, and Mendelian Randomization Reveal Ferroptosis-Related Molecular Subtypes and a Genetically Supported Causal Candidate in Psoriasis.
papers.authors: Xu M, Zuo Y, Liu H, Jia H, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Background Ferroptosis contributes to inflammatory skin diseases, but its role in psoriasis remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated multi‑omics analysis combining single‑cell transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, consensus clustering, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to characterize ferroptosis‑related molecular features, intercellular communication, immune microenvironment remodeling, molecular subtypes, and causal biomarkers in psoriasis. Methods Single‑cell RNA‑seq data (GSE151177) were analyzed to quantify ferroptosis activity across cell populations and infer intercellular communication networks. Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE30999, GSE78097) were integrated for differential expression and machine‑learning feature selection with SHAP interpretation. Consensus clustering, immune infiltration, functional enrichment, and drug repurposing analyses were performed. Cis‑eQTLs from eQTLGen (n=31,684) served as instruments for two‑sample MR with psoriasis GWAS from FinnGen (13,667 cases, 395,092 controls). Results Macrophages/monocytes and fibroblasts showed the highest ferroptosis scores. MIF signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44, MIF-CD74/CXCR4, MIF-ACKR3) dominated keratinocyte outgoing communication. Transcriptomic integration yielded 72 overlapping ferroptosis-related genes; machine learning identified eight feature genes (CD24, EFNB2, DDX39A, NDRG4, GPRC5A, S100A8, PRSS8, ITPKC). CD24 (AUC=0.979) and S100A8 (AUC=0.974) exhibited top diagnostic performance. Consensus clustering stratified patients into two subtypes (C1, C2); all eight genes were highly expressed in C1, while C2 showed upregulated phagocytic but downregulated innate immune pathways. Drug enrichment suggested MS-275, genistein, and β-adrenoceptor agonists as potential ferroptosis-modulating compounds. MR demonstrated that only PRSS8 eQTL had a nominally significant causal association with psoriasis risk ( P Conclusion Our multi‑omics study delineates the ferroptosis‑related landscape in psoriasis, identifies MIF signaling as a key keratinocyte communication axis, establishes a high‑performance diagnostic model with eight feature genes, defines two distinct immune‑metabolic subtypes, and provides genetic evidence supporting PRSS8 as a putative causal biomarker for psoriasis susceptibility, offering novel insights and potential ferroptosis‑based biomarkers and therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

papers.title: Bioinformatic design of ASC PYD-targeting peptides and preliminary cellular evaluation of their encoding mRNAs.
papers.authors: Karimian M, Kianmehr Z, Ghobeh M, Es-Haghi A.
papers.abstract: Inflammasome activation is central to innate immune signaling and inflammatory disorders. The adaptor protein ASC is a component of the inflammasome, and its Pyrin domain (PYD) mediates homotypic interactions involved in ASC oligomerization. Therefore, targeting the ASC PYD may modulate inflammasome-associated responses. In the present study, a structure-guided computational strategy was employed to design two candidate peptides, ASC1 and ASC2, targeting Interface I of the ASC PYD. The cryo-electron microscopy structure of the ASC PYD filament (PDB ID: 3J63) was used to identify an α-helical native template. Candidate sequence modifications were evaluated using ProDA and mmCSM-PPI servers, and the final peptide structures were generated using YASARA software. Peptide-ASC PYD complexes were assessed by 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations in GROMACS, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and interaction analysis using Discovery Studio Visualizer. The peptide-encoding sequences were transcribed in vitro into mRNA and transfected into Jurkat T-cells. Cellular responses following LPS/SiO 2 stimulation were evaluated using Annexin V-FITC/PI staining, DCFH-DA-based intracellular oxidative activity assays, and ELISA quantification of IL-1β and IL-18. The predicted ΔTOTAL values for ASC1, ASC2, and the Native template were -27.07, -22.97, and -9.16 kcal/mol, respectively, with ASC1 showing the most favorable predicted binding free energy. In Jurkat T-cells, ASC1- and ASC2-encoding mRNAs were associated with reduced apoptotic populations, decreased DCFH-associated intracellular oxidative activity, and lower IL-1β and IL-18 production following LPS/SiO 2 stimulation. ASC1 produced greater reductions in both cytokines than ASC2. ASC1 exhibited the most favorable computational and cytokine profiles and could be considered for further mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration.
papers.authors: Feng X, Chen HY, Sun Y, Sun F, Yan S, Kapuria S, Rodriguez R, Gamba L, Crump JG, Hong YK, Poss KD, Lien CL.
papers.abstract: Cardiac lymphatics regulate fluid homeostasis and immune cell clearance. The mechanisms underlying cardiac lymphatic vessel formation remain unclear. We perform spatial transcriptomics on the zebrafish heart at the single-cell level and investigate gene expression patterns in cardiac lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). adrenomedullin a (adma) is mainly expressed in the epicardium adjacent to cardiac lymphatics. adma mutants develop edema and dilated outflow tracts with mis-patterned and reduced lymphatics, while their ventricular lymphatics are dilated with fewer sprouts, increased lyve1b expression, and altered lymphatic subpopulation composition. Loss of ackr3a, which encodes an Adm decoy receptor, increases lymphatic sprouts. During heart regeneration, adma and ackr3a are expressed in epicardium-derived cells within the wound. Neutrophil clearance is reduced in adma mutants but increased in ackr3a mutants. Our findings uncover the heterogeneity of cardiac LECs and show that Adm and Ackr3 regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation in the zebrafish heart.

papers.title: The immunogenicity control axis: a multi-omics framework for integrating epigenetic, DNA damage response, and immune states in cancer.
papers.authors: Srivastava M, Singh S, Ameta D, Singh A, Banerjee M, Kushwah AS.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet therapeutic responses remain heterogeneous and are incompletely explained by immune-centric biomarkers alone. We propose the Immunogenicity Control Axis (ICA), a testable multi-omics framework integrating three complementary dimensions of tumor state: epigenetic regulation, DNA damage response (DDR), and immune activity. The central hypothesis is that epigenetic permissiveness influences immune-relevant transcription and antigen presentation, while DDR-associated genomic processes contribute to antigenic variation; together, these tumor-intrinsic features interact with the immune state to shape tumor immune visibility. To make this hypothesis quantitatively testable, the ICA is operationalized through independently derived Epigenetic, DDR, and Immune scores that are standardized and integrated into a composite ICA Score. Using cervical cancer as an initial disease context, patient-derived TCGA-CESC analyses provide exploratory assessment of ICA-associated molecular states and prognostic relationships, while synthetic analyses are used separately to illustrate specific analytical procedures. The framework is further extended to perturbational analysis, in which CMap/LINCS transcriptional signatures and network information are used to prioritize candidate natural compounds predicted to oppose ICA-associated molecular states. These computational analyses are intended as hypothesis-generating operationalizations rather than biological or clinical validation. ICA therefore provides a falsifiable framework for testing whether coordinated epigenetic, DDR, and immune information captures tumor immunogenic variation beyond individual molecular dimensions and for prioritizing perturbational hypotheses for subsequent experimental validation.

papers.title: Donor-aware multi-cohort single-cell analysis identifies an LXR-linked tubular cholesterol-handling state in membranous nephropathy with a coordinated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across renal tumors.
papers.authors: Mao Y, Li R, Li B, Pan H.
papers.abstract: Background Membranous nephropathy (MN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease in which sustained proteinuria exposes renal tubular epithelial cells to an abnormal filtered-protein load. The tubular metabolic response to this exposure remains incompletely characterized. We investigated whether MN is associated with a reproducible tubular cholesterol-handling transcriptional state and assessed its relationship to protein overload in vitro . We further evaluated whether an experimentally anchored five-gene subset showed a coordinated tumor-associated transcriptional shift across major renal cancer histologies. Methods Three kidney single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets and one glomerular bulk-transcriptomic cohort were analyzed using the donor as the biological replicate. GSE241302 was used for complete-case exploratory discovery, OEP004186 for formal donor-aware support, GSE171458 for directional support, and GSE200828 for tissue-level disease context. A frozen 47-gene LXR-linked cholesterol-handling program and its nested 37-gene cholesterol transport/efflux component were evaluated by donor-level pseudobulk analysis, leave-one-donor-out and leave-one-gene-out sensitivity analyses. HK-2 cells were exposed to protein overload, followed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR for representative transport and lipid-remodeling genes. The same experimentally anchored five-gene panel was then evaluated in 129 paired tumor-adjacent-normal samples across TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-KIRP, and TCGA-KICH to define a renal tumor-associated lipid-remodeling context. Results Across all 3 MN donors in GSE241302, program scores were higher than the internal reference in proximal tubule (PT) and loop-of-Henle/thick ascending limb (loop/TAL) compartments. In OEP004186, the program was increased in PT (effect +0.480, false-discovery rate [FDR] 0.0128), PT-VCAM1 (+0.348, FDR 0.0165), and loop/distal epithelial cells (+0.310, FDR 0.0242), with positive effects in every leave-one-MN-donor-out analysis. GSE171458 provided concordant directional support in PT and loop/TAL. The PT-VCAM1 fraction was not increased in MN, whereas the program remained higher within both PT and PT-VCAM1, favoring a within-state transcriptional change. Sixteen program genes showed positive average effects across the three single-cell resources. In GSE200828, the overall program was higher in MN than in living donors (+0.226, FDR 0.0349) but not higher than in other glomerular diseases. Protein overload increased ABCA1, ABCG1, SREBF1, FASN, and SCD expression in HK-2 cells. Across the three renal cancer histologies, the five-gene panel showed a concordant paired increase (REML-pooled effect +0.967, 95% CI 0.843-1.092), and 85.3% of patients exhibited simultaneous increases in the cholesterol-efflux and lipid-synthesis/remodeling arms. Conclusion MN is associated with a donor-supported LXR-linked cholesterol-handling transcriptional state concentrated in PT and loop/TAL-related epithelial compartments. The state is responsive to protein overload in HK-2 cells and may reflect a broader tubular lipid-homeostasis response to proteinuric kidney injury. The data do not establish direct LXR activation, increased cholesterol-efflux flux, or MN specificity. The paired renal cancer analysis further identifies a coordinated tumor-associated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across KIRC, KIRP, and KICH, while not establishing tumor-cell-intrinsic LXR activation, immune effects, or a causal tumor mechanism.

papers.title: Mechanisms of infantile hemangioma involution (Review).
papers.authors: Zheng X, Zeng Y, Liu J, Wang Y, Wen X, Peng W, Fu W, Liu H, Li Q, Chen F.
papers.abstract: Infantile hemangioma (IH) is the most common benign vascular tumor of infancy, characterized by a distinctive life cycle of rapid postnatal proliferation followed by spontaneous involution. However, the mechanisms underlying this regression process remain incompletely understood. In this narrative review, current IH-specific evidence was synthesized and candidate pathways were organized according to their relative strength. A total of three core mechanistic modules with moderate-to-high supporting evidence were identified: Endothelial proliferation restraint, immune microenvironment remodeling and adipogenic differentiation of hemangioma-derived progenitor cells. Additional pathways, including extracellular matrix remodeling, regulated cell death and endocrine signaling, were discussed as potential contributors but remain less validated. Overall, IH involution appears to represent an active and coordinated process of immunovascular remodeling rather than passive regression. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal human samples, single-cell and spatial profiling and functional validation in immune-competent models to clarify the temporal hierarchy and causal interactions among these pathways.

papers.title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
papers.authors: Zhang N, Wang C, Wang R, Guo X, Yu J, Wang J, Luo Q, Wu Y.
papers.abstract: Background Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns. Methods GEO datasets for IPAH and MPM were analyzed. Overlapping DEGs and WGCNA modules were identified. PPI network analysis combined with LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE was used to identify candidate biomarker genes. A classification model was constructed and evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Immune infiltration was evaluated by ssGSEA. Molecular docking and MD simulations assessed drug binding to candidate target proteins. qRT-PCR validated candidate biomarker gene expression. Results Six concordantly upregulated and eleven concordantly downregulated DEGs were shared between IPAH and MPM. Upregulated genes were enriched in cell cycle regulation, while downregulated genes were enriched in neutrophil chemotaxis. WGCNA identified 58 overlapping genes. CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 were identified as candidate biomarker genes. A ROTS sensitivity analysis confirmed that all 1710 MPM DEGs were reproducible and directionally concordant at the matching FDR Conclusion This hypothesis-generating study identifies shared transcriptomic signatures between IPAH and MPM, highlighting CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 as candidate biomarkers linked to immune dysregulation and metabolic reprogramming. The computational and correlative nature of these findings, together with the limited size of the external validation cohort, requires confirmation through functional experiments and validation in larger, independent, and multicentre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

papers.title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug-food homologous substance target prediction.
papers.authors: Liu D, Yan J, Luo T, Guo Y, Li Y, Long P, Yang L.
papers.abstract: Introduction High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug-food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown. Methods Datasets related to HA illness, as well as 106 DFH substances and their corresponding chemical components, were obtained in this study. Differentially expressed genes were identified, and active components were screened according to the criteria of drug-likeness ≥0.18 and oral bioavailability ≥30%. The GraphBAN tool was used to predict high-confidence compound-protein interaction pairs, so as to obtain the corresponding candidate active components and candidate genes. Meanwhile, the ADMETlab3 platform was employed to evaluate the druggability and toxicity of these active components, thereby determining the core active components and core genes. Candidate genes were screened were screened out by machine learning, and relevant interaction networks were constructed. Finally, further studies such as pathway enrichment, immune infiltration, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation were carried out. Results Of the 95 candidate active components subjected to toxicological screening, only 8 passed the safety evaluation, and 6 of these met both physicochemical and toxicological criteria; five candidate genes (DNAJC19, MRFAP1L1, TBPL1, RPS21, and NABP1) and two key active components (polyacetylene PQ-2, PQ-2) were identified, and these candidate genes corresponded to the DFH substance " Panacis Quinquefolii Radix ". The abovementioned candidate genes were enriched in pathways such as ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation, and they were correlated with most differential immune cells. Except for RPS21 and MRFAP1L1, the binding abilities of the other candidate genes with the key active components were good (binding energies Discussion Panacis Quinquefolii Radix might intervene in HA illness via active components (PQ-2) that target five candidate genes, regulating immunity and metabolism. This provided a preliminary computational basis for DFH-based HA illness prevention/treatment.

papers.title: Hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis of potential molecular convergence between a polystyrene oligomer proxy and papillary thyroid carcinoma.
papers.authors: Xie W, Tang J, Qian X.
papers.abstract: Background Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) are emerging environmental contaminants with endocrine-disrupting and pro-inflammatory effects, but whether PS-MPs-associated molecular targets converge with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) alterations remains unclear. This hypothesis-generating study aimed to identify candidate molecular networks and cellular contexts shared between a simplified polystyrene computational proxy and PTC. Methods Putative targets from CTD and from TargetNet/SwissTargetPrediction using a five-styrene-unit oligomer proxy were intersected with thyroid cancer-related genes from OMIM and GeneCards. Protein functional-association and enrichment analyses were followed by differential expression analysis in GSE33630 (45 normal and 49 PTC samples). LASSO and SVM-RFE identified core genes; stability was examined by repeated nested resampling conditional on the seven-gene candidate panel. Individual-gene tumor-normal discrimination was assessed in GSE33630 and GSE60542. Protein patterns were evaluated qualitatively in the Human Protein Atlas and preliminarily in 15 matched PTC-adjacent tissue pairs. CIBERSORT-estimated immune fractions and two single-cell datasets were analyzed as exploratory context. Results Among 144 putative proxy-associated targets and 2,139 thyroid cancer-related genes, 75 were shared. Seven candidates overlapped with 1,306 PTC differentially expressed genes, and BCL2, BAX, and FN1 were selected by both feature-selection methods and remained stable across the tested GeneCards thresholds and CTD-only sensitivity analysis. BCL2 was downregulated, whereas BAX and FN1 were upregulated in PTC; individual-gene AUCs were 0.963, 0.941, and 0.965 in GSE33630 and 0.942, 0.907, and 0.955 in GSE60542. HPA images and clinical IHC supported the same protein-level directions. After multiple-testing correction, only the CIBERSORT-estimated neutrophil fraction differed between groups (higher in PTC; q=0.0021). Single-cell analysis localized the three genes across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments. Conclusion BCL2, BAX, and FN1 are candidate molecular nodes at the convergence of polystyrene-proxy annotations and PTC-associated alterations. The findings do not demonstrate patient PS-MPs exposure, intact-particle effects, or causality, and require validation in material-characterized exposure experiments and exposure-aware clinical studies.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomics with reverse network pharmacology prioritizes macrophage-associated candidate genes in Lyme arthritis.
papers.authors: Dong Y, Luo Y, Chen Y, Liu M, Zhou Y, Yang Y, Chen X, Yang F, Liang Z, Zi L, Gao H, Cao Z, Gao F, Song C, Zhou G.
papers.abstract: Introduction Lyme arthritis (LA) involves complex immune dysregulation, and macrophages contribute centrally to persistent joint inflammation. However, synovial macrophage heterogeneity and its potential relevance to therapeutic intervention remain incompletely defined. Methods We integrated scRNA-seq data from Borrelia burgdorferi ( Bb )-infected murine joints (GSE233850) with bulk RNA-seq data (GSE283617). The workflow included Seurat clustering, Monocle 3 trajectory inference, CellChat communication analysis, and functional enrichment. We constructed a PPI network from intersecting genes and applied five complementary topological measures to prioritize consensus hubs. Candidate gene expression was evaluated in an external transcriptomic dataset (GSE63085) and by qRT-PCR. CTD-based association analysis and molecular docking were used to prioritize candidate compounds. Virtual knockout analysis explored the potential regulatory effects of hub genes. Results The two pooled libraries differed descriptively in the relative representation of nine major cell populations. Among macrophages/monocytes, we resolved seven marker-defined states. Monocle 3 trajectories were rooted at Classical_Inflam_Mono, and CellChat highlighted Tgfb1-(Tgfbr1+Tgfbr2) as a prominent inferred TGF-β axis. Intersecting GSE283617 with GSE233850 yielded 121 shared genes, and GSEA showed negative enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation during infection. Mrc1 and Msr1 were the only genes ranked among the top 10 by all five measures: Degree, Bottleneck, EcCentricity, MNC, and MCC. Across these complementary analyses, Msr1 emerged as a candidate Bb -responsive gene potentially relevant to LA. A CTD-based source-compound-gene network and molecular docking prioritized curcumin and demethoxycurcumin for future experimental testing. Conclusion These findings provide an exploratory atlas of macrophage transcriptional states in the analyzed LA model and identify Msr1 as a candidate infection-responsive gene. Its disease specificity and clinical utility require validation in joint-derived specimens from patients with clinically confirmed LA. The computationally prioritized compounds remain hypotheses that require direct binding and functional testing.

papers.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation.
papers.authors: Yu S, Xu D, Hua Y, Mo H, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis. Objective Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis. Methods We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the in vitro assay identified expression patterns of the main contributor. Results KM-associated molecular patterns can potentially guide the diagnostic and molecular stratification for DMD patients. USP18 can be considered an upregulated and mast cell-distributed hub gene involved in pathogenesis of DMD. In addition, finafloxacin with BRD-K10482608 can be considered two potential therapeutic candidates for DMD patient clinical applications. Conclusion Our investigation described a novel forecasting and therapeutic model for DMD patients, which potentially enhances DMD patient clinical translation.

papers.title: Dynamic remodeling of microglial responses in Alzheimer's disease: heterogeneous states, spatiotemporal progression, and immunometabolic dysregulation.
papers.authors: Han S, Wang S, Liu J, Liu X, Wang Q, Meng C.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neuroinflammation involving microglia whose functional responses extend far beyond the classical M1/M2 framework and form a dynamically heterogeneous continuum. Here, we review recurrent disease-associated microglia (DAM) states and transcriptional programs, including DAM-associated, interferon-responsive, cytokine-responsive, proliferative, antigen-presentation-associated, and lipid-associated features, emphasizing that these labels do not necessarily represent fixed or mutually exclusive cellular subtypes. Across AD progression, the relative engagement and functional consequences of these programs vary according to Aβ and tau burden, local microenvironment, genetic background, metabolic status, and disease stage. DAM-associated programs may support phagocytosis and plaque containment in some contexts, whereas persistent inflammatory and metabolic stress can increase lipid dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired phagocytic competence, and inflammatory signaling in subsets of microglia. Microglia also exert bidirectional effects on tau pathology. Core AD risk pathways, including TREM2 and APOE, together with immunometabolic remodeling, shape microglial plasticity in a context-dependent manner. We discuss the implications of this dynamic framework for stage- and state-aware therapeutic strategies and highlight the need to integrate single-cell, spatial, and multi-omic approaches to resolve microglial trajectories and functional states in human AD.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Human CD46 humanized mice reveal interferon associated pulmonary immune remodeling during human adenovirus type 7 lung infection.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Meng Z, Wan M, Lu Y, Rao L, Qu H, Wei J, Liao J, Liu E, Zang N.
papers.abstract: Background Human adenovirus type 7(HAdV-7) is a major cause of severe pediatric pneumonia, but the mechanisms linking viral infection to pulmonary immune remodeling and lung pathology remain incompletely understood. Progress has been limited by the lack of physiologically relevant animal models that recapitulate human susceptibility. Methods We generated human CD46 (hCD46) humanized mice and evaluated pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virus, and lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues from wild type and hCD46 humanized mice under control and infected conditions to characterize cellular composition, transcriptional states, and intercellular communication. Human PBMC bulk transcriptomes from pediatric HAdV infection were further analyzed to assess the systemic relevance of mouse lung derived immune programs. Results hCD46 humanized mice showed increased pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virions, and more severe lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell profiling revealed depletion of resident alveolar macrophages, pronounced expansion of inflammatory macrophage subsets, and remodeling of lymphoid transcriptional states in infected hCD46 lungs. These changes were accompanied by prominent type I/II interferon and interferon associated chemokine programs. B cells and CD4 + and CD8 + T cells showed prominent interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) associated transcriptional states, together with alterations in selected effector- and memory-associated programs and computationally inferred trajectories. Projection of mouse lung derived signatures onto transcriptomes of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell showed that selected interferon associated myeloid and lymphoid programs were also detectable systemically in pediatric HAdV infection. Conclusions HAdV-7 infection in hCD46 humanized mice was associated with an interferon enriched pulmonary inflammatory environment, prominent inflammatory myeloid remodeling, and altered lymphoid transcriptional states. This susceptible mouse model provides a useful experimental tool for studying HAdV-7 associated lung disease and for preclinical evaluation of antiviral, immunomodulatory, and vaccine strategies.

papers.title: Neutrophil heterogeneity under IL-17A deficiency in experimental periodontitis.
papers.authors: Tang Z, Hu R, Zhu L, Hu J, Xiao F, Jin L, Lu L, Yang Y.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a dysbiotic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive periodontal destruction, in which neutrophils play a central but functionally diverse role. IL-17A is closely linked to neutrophil-mediated host responses; however, how IL-17A deficiency reshapes neutrophil heterogeneity during periodontitis remains unclear. Here, we established a Porphyromonas gingivalis -induced experimental periodontitis model in wild-type and IL-17A knockout mice and integrated micro-CT, histology, 16S rRNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing to define the consequences of IL-17A loss in the periodontal microenvironment. IL-17A deficiency exacerbated alveolar bone loss and osteoclast accumulation and was associated with altered oral microbial composition consistent with dysbiosis. Single-cell profiling revealed marked remodeling of the immune landscape, with impaired neutrophil accumulation and altered neutrophil subset composition in IL-17A-deficient periodontal tissues. Neutrophils from IL-17A knockout mice showed reduced inflammatory chemokine/cytokine programs and a shift toward antimicrobial granule-associated, extracellular matrix-responsive, and TGF-β/THBS-linked transcriptional states. Trajectory, transcriptional regulatory, and cell-cell communication analyses further demonstrated that IL-17A deficiency disrupted neutrophil state transitions and attenuated neutrophil-centered CCL, CXCL, TNF, SELPG, and ICAM signaling while enhancing matrix-associated communication pathways. Together, these findings identify IL-17A deficiency as a driver of neutrophil reprogramming and aggravated periodontal destruction and indicate an association with microbial dysbiosis, providing single-cell-level insight into the IL-17A-neutrophil axis in dysbiotic periodontitis.

papers.title: Neonatal outcomes and immune reprogramming induced by prenatal opioid and hepatitis C exposure.
papers.authors: Doratt BM, True HE, Wagner SB, Malherbe DC, Cockerham C, O'Brien J, Messaoudi I.
papers.abstract: Introduction Prenatal opioid exposure (POE) is an escalating public health concern. However, its impact on neonatal immune development remains poorly defined. This study examined how POE, with or without maternal hepatitis C (hepatitis C virus, HCV) infection, shapes neonatal immunity. Methods Umbilical cord blood was collected from pregnancies included uncomplicated term controls (n=38) and deliveries in patients with severe opioid use disorder on medication-assisted treatment, with (n=41) or without HCV (n=34) infection. Flow cytometry was used to characterize cell phenotype and functional response to stimulation. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate transcriptomics changes. Results POE was associated with smaller birth size, higher rates of congenital anomalies, and longer intensive care admissions. Immune profiling showed a proinflammatory milieu, reduced circulating levels of neuroprotective factors, expanded memory/effector T and B cells, blunted T-cell responses, and markedly reduced natural killer (NK) cell frequency and cytotoxicity, especially in POE HCV+ newborns. Monocytes exhibited inflammatory reprogramming with impaired antiviral and tissue repair pathways and disrupted lymphoid-innate immune cell communication. Discussion These findings suggest that POE-driven immune disequilibrium may underlie adverse early-life outcomes and highlight monitoring and intervention targets.

papers.title: A CD68-expressing tissue-homing subset in peripheral CD8 + T cells predicts response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Huang J, Sun Z, Pei Y, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Background T-cell function is regulated by immunometabolism, and lysosomes are signaling hubs. CD68 (LAMP4), traditionally regarded as a monocyte/macrophage marker, has been largely neglected in T cell biology. We aimed to assess the link between CD68 expression in T cells and anti-PD-1 response in lung cancer, and its potential as an early dynamic biomarker in peripheral blood CD8 + T cells. Methods We analyzed transcriptomic (GSE126044, GSE135222, GSE166449) and single-cell (GSE207422) data from anti-PD-1-treated lung cancer cohorts to identify lysosome related pathways and key genes, validated with peripheral blood CD8 + T cell data (GSE111414). Prospectively, we enrolled lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, collecting peripheral blood at baseline and week 3. Flow cytometry measured CD68 in CD8 + T cells and subsets, assessing association with response, progression-free survival (PFS), and functional markers (granzyme B, perforin, Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, IL-1β). Results Responders showed enrichment of lysosome pathways and upregulation of 8 lysosome related genes including CD68, positively correlated with monocyte and T cell infiltration. Single-cell data linked CD68 expression in T cell to favorable response. After one cycle, the proportion of CD8 + CD68 + T cells was lower in non-responders ( P ), with AUC 0.803 ( P=0.044 ) and cutoff 1.015%, stratifying PFS ( P=0.0225 ). CD68 was highest in naïve T cells at baseline, but decreased across subsets after treatment in non-responders (all P ). Functionally, compared with CD8 + CD68 - T cells, CD8 + CD68 + T cells exhibited lower expression of granzyme B and perforin but higher expression of Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, and IL-1β (all P ), suggesting a CD8 + T cell state characterized by lower cytotoxicity and enhanced proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, accompanied by a tissue residency associated phenotype. Conclusion CD8 + CD68 + T cells exhibit lower cytotoxicity but greater proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, together with a tissue residency associated phenotype, suggesting a precursor-like state. Low CD68 expression in tumor-infiltrating T cells and the post-treatment reduction of CD68 expression in peripheral blood CD8 + T cells are associated with resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer. These findings suggest that CD8 + CD68 + T cells may serve as a potential early dynamic immune biomarker for monitoring and assessing response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analyses define neuronal heterogeneity and PDIA4-associated malignancy in glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Luo X, Deng X, Liu Y, Wu W.
papers.abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by extensive cellular heterogeneity and complex interactions between malignant cells and the surrounding microenvironment. The contribution of neuronal populations to GBM progression and prognosis, however, remains incompletely understood. Methods Bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA-GBM and GTEx were integrated with two single-cell RNA-seq datasets. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine-learning-based survival modeling, CIBERSORT, GSEA, CopyKAT, MiloR, pseudotime analysis, GSVA, CellChat, and pySCENIC were used to characterize prognostic genes and their cellular context. PDIA4 was further examined in U251 and U87 cells using siRNA-mediated knockdown followed by Western blotting, qPCR, Transwell invasion, wound-healing, colony-formation, and CCK-8 assays. Results Nine prognostic genes-PDIA4, CAMK2N1, RPH3A, RAB11FIP4, DMTN, EPHB6, SLC47A2, ESM1, and EMILIN2-were retained in the final prognostic model. Single-cell analysis showed distinct cellular distributions of these genes and identified a tumor-associated neuronal population enriched in GBM. Pseudotime analysis revealed transcriptional differences between normal- and tumor-associated neuronal states, while CellChat predicted altered NRXN-NLGN communication involving neuronal populations and GBM cells. Immune deconvolution showed associations between several prognostic genes and immune-cell composition, including an inverse correlation between PDIA4 and activated NK cells. Experimentally, PDIA4 was expressed at higher levels in U251 and U87 cells than in SVG p12 cells. PDIA4 knockdown reduced clonogenic growth, invasion, wound closure, and CCK-8 metabolic activity readouts in both GBM cell lines. Conclusions Integrative bulk and single-cell analyses linked GBM prognosis to distinct neuronal and immune features of the tumor microenvironment. Together, these analyses place the nine-gene prognostic signature within the cellular architecture of GBM and highlight tumor-associated neuronal states as a potential component of the prognostic tumor ecosystem. PDIA4 knockdown provided complementary functional support for one component of the signature, while the predicted NRXN-NLGN network nominates a candidate route of neuron-GBM communication for future investigation.

papers.title: Engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells for hematological malignancies: genome editing, synthetic biology, and precision immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Bahr AR, Basem Y, Alhejely A, Alaa AR, Abozeid SM, Basem A, Khormi MA, Abo-Zaid MA.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment by enabling engineered immune cells to selectively recognize and eliminate malignant targets, with CAR-T cells establishing the first major clinical success in this field. However, severe associated toxicities, logistical complexities of autologous manufacturing, and high rates of antigen-loss relapse have accelerated the development of alternative effector platforms such as CAR-NK cells. CAR-NK cells combine antigen-directed cytotoxicity with the innate antitumor functions of natural killer cells, offering a potentially safer and more readily available off-the-shelf therapeutic strategy. Nevertheless, the clinical efficacy of CAR-NK therapy is constrained by key biological and translational hurdles: brief in vivo persistence, inadequate trafficking and solid tumor infiltration, severe susceptibility to tumor microenvironment-mediated immunosuppression, and antigen escape driven by tumor heterogeneity. These biological constraints are compounded by technical bottlenecks, including cell source variability, limited large-scale expansion capacity, ex vivo functional exhaustion, and an absence of standardized manufacturing protocols. To address these multi-faceted barriers, recent advances in genome engineering, systems biology, and computational modeling provide promising routes forward. Given that prolonged exposure to immunosuppressive niches induces functional impairment, genome-editing strategies targeting inhibitory checkpoints and persistence programs are crucial; however, enhancing persistence requires stringent safeguards to mitigate toxicity risks from constitutive signaling or genomic instability. Thus, engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells necessitates balancing extended longevity, potent cytotoxicity, and safety. Multiomics approaches facilitate deeper characterization of CAR-NK functional states and tumor-immune interactions, whereas artificial intelligence-guided engineering integrates high-dimensional biological and manufacturing data to optimize receptor design, predict therapeutic performance, and accelerate translational workflows. Collectively, these innovations support a paradigm shift toward programmable CAR-NK cells that can dynamically sense, adapt, and respond to tumor evolution, driving the transition toward autonomous, highly scalable, and precisely controllable cellular immunotherapies in precision oncology.

papers.title: TREM-1 deficiency attenuates RIPK3/MLKL-associated epithelial injury in Klebsiella pneumoniae -induced acute lung injury.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Meng S, Huang J, Xiao E, Bai Y, Zhao L, Wang K.
papers.abstract: Background Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP)-induced acute lung injury involves excessive myeloid inflammation, epithelial barrier disruption, and inflammatory cell death. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM-1) amplifies innate immune responses, whereas receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling contributes to membrane injury. Their relationship during bacterial lung infection remains incompletely understood. Methods KP-induced acute lung injury was established in wild-type and Trem1 -deficient mice, and GSK872 was administered prophylactically to inhibit RIPK3. Lung histopathology, inflammatory mediators, and RIPK3/MLKL activation were assessed. Two human lung single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets containing non-fibrotic and fibrotic tissues were analyzed as cross-disease, hypothesis-generating reference cohorts. In vitro , conditioned medium from KP-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophage-like cells was applied to BEAS-2B epithelial cells; macrophage TREM-1 was blocked with LP17, and epithelial RIPK3 was silenced using siRNA. Results KP challenge increased pulmonary TREM-1 abundance and was accompanied by histopathological injury and altered inflammatory mediator concentrations. Trem1 deficiency reduced these responses together with RIPK3 and MLKL phosphorylation. Prophylactic GSK872 administration produced changes in the same direction. In the human fibrosis reference cohorts, TREM1 was concentrated in inflammatory myeloid populations, and ligand-receptor inference identified candidate macrophage-to-epithelial communication pathways. In vitro , KP increased TREM-1 and inflammatory mediator release from macrophage-like cells. Their conditioned medium induced epithelial membrane injury, RIPK3/MLKL phosphorylation, and loss of E-cadherin and ZO-1; these effects were attenuated by macrophage LP17 pretreatment or epithelial RIPK3 knockdown. Conclusion Trem1 deficiency attenuated KP-induced acute lung injury and was associated with reduced pulmonary inflammation and RIPK3/MLKL activation. The combined findings support a functional relationship between macrophage TREM-1-dependent inflammatory activation and epithelial RIPK3/MLKL-associated injury, rather than a fully established linear signaling axis. This intercellular injury network warrants further mechanistic and post-infection therapeutic evaluation.

papers.title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation.
papers.authors: Kong M, Guan X, Jing Y, Xie Z, Zhao X, Huang S, Yu Y, Zhang C.
papers.abstract: Background Glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) represent a recently recognized connection between RNA biology and cell-surface glycobiology. However, whether glycoRNA-related processes are relevant to human tumors remains unclear, partly because direct glycoRNA measurements are not yet available across large cancer cohorts. We therefore used transcriptomic data to identify tumor settings in which glycoRNA-related programs may be most suitable for further experimental validation. Methods We curated a glycoRNA-focused literature evidence base and manually reviewed the top extracted relations to define gene modules related to RNA identity, N-glycan and sialylation pathways, RNA trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. The glycoRNA-related cellular program score is an expression-based composite score representing coordinated glycoRNA-related cellular programs, including RNA processing, glycan biosynthesis, trafficking, and lectin/Siglec recognition. It is designed to prioritize tumor contexts for experimental glycoRNA validation. The score was applied to 9,186 TCGA tumors from 32 cancer types and analyzed together with clinical variables, leukocyte fraction, immune signatures, Siglec/checkpoint/myeloid-axis scores, and non-overlapping sensitivity models. Glioblastoma single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets were used for additional context-level validation. Results Higher glycoRNA-related cellular program scores were observed in several tumor types, including stomach adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, mesothelioma, pancreatic adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, and lung squamous carcinoma. Survival analyses did not show robust FDR-significant associations after adjustment for age, sex, stage, and tumor type, suggesting that the score should not be interpreted as a general prognostic biomarker. In sensitivity analyses that removed immune and Siglec-related genes from the predictor, the score remained associated with Siglec-decoder, myeloid, checkpoint, and integrated niche features after adjustment for leukocyte fraction and cancer-type effects. Within-cancer meta-analysis supported these associations across cancer types, although effect sizes varied. In glioblastoma, higher scores were found in tumor, myeloid, mesenchymal, and niche-associated compartments in single-cell and spatial analyses. Conclusions This study presents an expression-based map of glycoRNA-related cellular program across human cancers. The results suggest that glycoRNA-related transcriptional programs tend to occur in immune- and myeloid-enriched tumor microenvironments, particularly those involving Siglec-associated features. These findings prioritize tumor contexts for biochemical, imaging, spatial, and perturbation-based glycoRNA validation.

papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts in triple-negative breast cancer: heterogeneity, tumor-stroma crosstalk, and therapeutic resistance.
papers.authors: Wei S, Xie X, Cao Y, Wei L.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) comprises a clinically and biologically heterogeneous group of breast cancers defined by the absence of estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor expression and the lack of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) overexpression or amplification. Although systemic treatment has expanded beyond chemotherapy to include immune checkpoint blockade, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition in selected patients with germline BRCA1/2 variants, and antibody-drug conjugates in advanced disease, therapeutic resistance and disease recurrence remain major challenges. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are abundant stromal cells that contribute to the organization and function of the TNBC microenvironment. Rather than representing a single uniformly tumor-promoting population, CAFs encompass transcriptionally and functionally diverse states that vary across tumors, spatial niches, and treatment contexts. Current evidence supports roles for selected CAF populations in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, paracrine signaling, metabolic exchange, immune-cell positioning, and adaptation to therapeutic stress. Recent single-cell and spatial studies have further identified ECM-rich, inflammatory, hypoxia-associated, and progenitor-like fibroblast states that correlate with distinct immune landscapes and treatment responses. However, many proposed CAF markers are shared across states, nomenclature remains inconsistent among datasets, and most CAF-directed therapeutic strategies are supported primarily by preclinical evidence. This review summarizes the current understanding of CAF heterogeneity in TNBC, examines the mechanisms through which fibroblast states influence tumor progression and antitumor immunity, and critically evaluates their contribution to chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance. Particular attention is given to the distinction between mechanistic evidence and associative transcriptomic findings, as well as to the translational challenges that must be addressed before CAF-based biomarkers or therapies can be incorporated into routine TNBC management.

papers.title: A redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulation: a hypothesis on NLRP3-Mediated regulation.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Wang D, Lin Q, Guo P, Wang Z.
papers.abstract: Ovulation is a highly coordinated biological process involving endocrine regulation, tissue remodeling, immune activation, metabolic adaptation, and redox signaling. Although inflammatory responses are recognized as essential components of follicular rupture, the mechanisms integrating oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and inflammasome activation during ovulatory progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose a hypothesis-driven redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulatory regulation, in which NLRP3 inflammasome signaling may serve as an important integrator of redox and metabolic cues that modulate inflammatory remodeling during the periovulatory period. This model suggests that successful ovulation requires a precisely balanced inflammatory threshold, whereas insufficient or excessive inflammasome activation may disrupt follicular homeostasis and contribute to ovarian dysfunction. Importantly, NLRP3 is proposed not as an indispensable determinant of follicular rupture, but as one regulatory component within a complex network involving cytokines, prostaglandins, matrix metalloproteinases, immune cells, and hormonal signals. By integrating current evidence linking mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, metabolic stress, and inflammation, this hypothesis provides a conceptual framework for understanding ovulation as a redox-sensitive immune-metabolic process. Future studies using cell type-specific NLRP3 manipulation, quantitative redox analysis, and single-cell approaches will be required to determine the physiological contribution of inflammasome signaling to ovulatory regulation.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal immune remodeling by light at night uncovers an adaptive immune signature linked to tumor progression and anti-PD-1 non-response.
papers.authors: Cheng K, Kong R, Zhang H, Nie Z, Gao Q, Du C, Cai L, Li Q, Liu S, Sheng H.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption, notably induced by light at night (LAN), is increasingly recognized as a modulator of systemic immune function; however, its high-resolution spatiotemporal impact and relevance to cancer immunotherapy remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed a spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas of murine lymph nodes, peripheral blood, and spleen across circadian time points to dissect the immunological consequences of LAN exposure. We observed that LAN exposure was associated with profound, tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling of the adaptive immune system. Specifically, B cells exhibited suppressed circadian clock programs and impaired homing and retention signatures. Concurrently, CD8 + T cells exhibited transcriptional profiles consistent with an aberrantly activated, late-effector state, a transition accompanied by altered intercellular MHC-I communication. To evaluate the translational relevance of these transcriptomic shifts, we developed a computational LAN Immune Dyssynchrony Score (LAN-IDS) and projected these murine-derived signatures onto human cancer cohorts. In human melanoma sentinel lymph nodes, the LAN-associated CD8 + T cell trajectory exhibited strong directional concordance with advanced (Stage III) disease. Crucially, interrogating these signatures within a clinical melanoma cohort revealed that the aberrantly activated CD8 + T cell program is significantly elevated in patients with primary resistance to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Collectively, our cross-species computational analysis identifies a spatiotemporal adaptive immune dyssynchrony signature. These findings identify specific lymphocyte transcriptional states that may serve as candidate correlates of tumor progression and immunotherapy non-response.

papers.title: Single-Cell Sequencing of Diffuse Midline Glioma Reveals That CTHRC1 Promotes Tumor Malignant Progression via the Wnt/β-Catenin/MMP2 Signaling Pathway.
papers.authors: Gao Y, Yu Z, Xie Y, Chen L, Shi L, Zhu R, Lu Y.
papers.abstract: Despite the continuous advancement of neurosurgical techniques and the accelerated pace of drug development, the prognosis of diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains unsatisfactory. Reports on the cellular atlas and biological characteristics of DMG remain relatively scarce. With the rapid development of biotechnology, especially single-cell transcriptome technology, people's understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME) of DMG can be effectively enhanced. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of single-cell transcriptome profiles from 3 DMG samples collected from our center to investigate the characteristics of intratumoral heterogeneity and the TME. As a core component of DMG tumor cells, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) are predominantly localized in the cellular tumor (CT) region, whereas OPCs in the leading edge (LE) and microvascular proliferation (MVP) regions contribute to immune suppression. The pseudotime trajectory of monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) demonstrates that they infiltrate the tumor tissues via the microvascular proliferation (MVP) and leading edge (LE) regions, and then migrate toward the tumor core (CT) or pseudo-palisading cells around necrosis (PAN) regions, which is correlated with tumor immune suppression. In addition, CTHRC1 can promote the malignant progression of DMG via the Wnt/β-catenin/MMP2 signaling pathway. Together, our work provides an in-depth understanding of the microenvironment of DMG, thereby laying a framework for uncovering targeted therapeutic strategies for DMG.

papers.title: Growth Hormone-Related Gene Signatures Reveal Diagnostic Biomarkers, Immune Landscapes, and Potential Therapeutic Targets in Sepsis Through WGCNA and Machine Learning Analyses.
papers.authors: Li X, Liu A, Ding Y, Chen G, Zhang B.
papers.abstract: Background Sepsis reshapes inflammatory, immune, and metabolic activity, yet the behavior of genes linked to growth hormone biology within this response has not been well defined. We therefore searched for growth hormone-related genes (GHRGs) that could distinguish sepsis and asked whether the resulting markers also reflected variation in host immune state. Methods For model development, two Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) microarray cohorts were combined, while GSE26378 and GSE28750 were kept separate for validation. Sepsis-associated expression signals were first defined by differential analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), then intersected with 1205 GHRGs. A protein-protein interaction step and four machine-learning procedures were used to reduce the candidate set. Classification was examined with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and a two-gene nomogram, with calibration and decision-curve analyses used as complementary checks. We also examined pathway enrichment, immune-cell patterns, predicted regulatory interactions, candidate compounds, and expression-based molecular subgroups. Results The integrated cohort yielded 2552 DEGs and 1873 genes from sepsis-associated WGCNA modules; their overlap with the GHRG collection contained 40 genes. PPI module analysis reduced this set to 23 hub candidates. Machine-learning screening consistently retained JAK1 and GATA3, both of which were downregulated in sepsis and showed stable diagnostic performance across the training and external validation cohorts. Their combined model provided stronger discrimination than either gene alone. Functional analyses linked the two genes to T-cell signaling, antigen processing, immune regulation, mitochondrial metabolism, and translational processes. Immune profiling revealed reduced lymphocyte-associated features together with enhanced myeloid signatures in sepsis. When septic samples were grouped by JAK1/GATA3 expression, two subtypes with different immune and transcriptional profiles emerged. Conclusions JAK1 and GATA3 emerged as promising growth hormone-related candidate diagnostic biomarkers associated with immune heterogeneity in sepsis. Their combined signature may provide a useful framework for molecular stratification and warrants further experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Age-Associated Cellular and Transcriptional Changes in Murine Lacrimal Glands.
papers.authors: Huang D, Si H, Jiao X, Xuan S, Yang T, Ba M, Qi D, Pei X, Lu D, Huang S, Liu X, Li Z.
papers.abstract: Purpose To characterize age-associated changes in lacrimal gland cellular composition, transcriptional states, and intercellular communication and to explore their relationship with lacrimal gland dysfunction and age-related dry eye disease (DED). Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on extraorbital lacrimal glands from young (12-week-old) and aged (20-month-old) male C57BL/6J mice. A total of 47,537 high-quality cells were analyzed using the Seurat pipeline. Differential expression, pathway enrichment (gene set enrichment analysis), and cell-cell communication (CellChat) analyses were used to assess aging-associated changes in immune composition and signaling dynamics. Results Aging was associated with pronounced immune-cell infiltration accompanied by epithelial and stromal remodeling, with higher observed representation of T cells, B cells, and plasma cells and broad transcriptional alterations across immune populations. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) increased in frequency but exhibited transcriptional profiles suggestive of reduced suppressive capacity. Aged T cells showed enrichment for Th1, Th2, and Th17 differentiation pathways. Also, γδ T cells formed a distinct Th17-skewed subset, and type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) expanded with stress-adaptive reprogramming. Migratory dendritic cells and macrophages exhibited activation of Janus kinase (JAK)-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT), tumor necrosis factor (TNF), and FoxO signaling. CellChat analysis revealed enhanced programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) signaling and T-cell-centric communication, alongside diminished homeostatic interactions. Conclusions Aging disrupts lacrimal gland immune homeostasis through coordinated remodeling of lymphoid, myeloid, and stromal compartments. These changes are associated with chronic inflammation and fibrosis and parallel mucosal immune aging observed in other mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues such as the gut and lung. This high-resolution, single-cell atlas highlights IL-6/transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), JAK-STAT, PD-L1, and FoxO signaling as candidate pathways for further investigation, providing a framework for future mechanistic studies and therapeutic exploration in aging-associated DED.

papers.title: PLXNB2 Regulates Monocyte-Mediated Inflammation and Intercellular Communication in the Pathogenesis of Diabetic Retinopathy.
papers.authors: Wang Q, Zhang P, Ji F, Li Y, Lu P.
papers.abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes, with a complex pathogenesis in which inflammatory responses and abnormal intercellular communication play pivotal roles. As crucial immune cells, monocytes play a central role in the inflammatory processes of DR by secreting various signaling molecules and interacting with other retinal cells, thereby jointly driving disease progression. However, the key molecules that regulate monocyte function and intercellular communication in DR remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to investigate the role of PLXNB2 in the pathogenesis of DR, particularly its regulatory effects on monocyte-mediated inflammation and intercellular communication. The novelty of this study lies in the integration of WGCNA, differential expression analysis, machine learning, SHAP interpretation, single-cell transcriptomics, and cell-cell communication analysis to systematically identify PLXNB2 as a potential regulator of monocyte-associated inflammation in DR. Methods This study employed bioinformatics approaches to systematically identify candidate genes associated with DR. WGCNA was leveraged to construct gene co-expression networks using DR and NDR samples, and differential gene expression analysis was performed to identify gene modules and key genes associated with DR. Subsequently, functional enrichment analysis was conducted on the relevant genes. Machine learning, in conjunction with SHAP value analysis, was employed to accurately screen for key genes driving the DR phenotype. To further investigate cellular mechanisms, single-cell transcriptomic and cell-cell communication analyses were performed, focusing on monocyte characteristics and intercellular signaling in DR patient samples. Ultimately, this study identified and focused on PLXNB2 as a candidate molecule potentially involved in monocyte-mediated inflammation and pathological intercellular communication in DR. Results After comprehensive gene screening using WGCNA, machine learning, and single-cell transcriptomics, PLXNB2 was found to be the most important gene. PLXNB2 showed strong diagnostic relevance for distinguishing DR from NDR samples and was identified by SHAP analysis as a major contributor to the model prediction. It was discovered that its expression level was closely related to the improvement of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). Single-cell analysis showed that PLXNB2 significantly altered the molecular landscape of monocytes, and there were clear enhancements in the expression patterns of their genes. Single-cell transcription may have an association with Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), but it does not demonstrate that PLXNB2 causes transcriptional remodeling. Discussion Our findings indicate that PLXNB2 can serve as a diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target for DR. Mechanistically, PLXNB2 may regulate monocyte communication via the ANXA1-FPR1 ligand-receptor pair, mediating anti-inflammatory pathways to inhibit inflammation and cell migration, and participating in apoptotic clearance as well as immune cell chemotaxis and activation, thereby providing mechanistic evidence for PLXNB2 as a therapeutic target for DR. Conclusion This integrative multi-omics analysis identifies PLXNB2 as a promising monocyte- associated biomarker linked to inflammatory regulation and altered intercellular communication in diabetic retinopathy.
